card: Negating startup arguments via -nofoo or -foo=0 frequently produces surprising or broken behavior because Bitcoin Core records negated options as the string "0". This PR adds an opt-in NEGATE_TO_EMPTY flag for string options, disallows negating options where negation is meaningless, enforces minimum cluster limits, evaluates boolean options like -cjdnsreachable and -help by boolean value rather than presence, and requires -nolistenonion if -notorcontrol is used. This fixes an assertion crash in TxGraph when starting with -nolimitclustercount, stops -norpcpassword from setting an RPC password of "0", prevents notify commands from executing a binary named "0", and avoids -notorcontrol dialing 0.0.0.0:9051.
changed_since_previous: Replaced NEGATE_TO_DEFAULT with NEGATE_TO_EMPTY so negated string options return "" instead of their default value. Changed -notorcontrol to require explicit -nolistenonion at startup instead of automatically disabling onion listening. Explicitly disallowed negation for -blocksdir and -walletdir with DISALLOW_NEGATION instead of falling back to default directories.
evidence: PR description: '-nolimitclustercount hits an assertion in TxGraph on the first mempool transaction. -nolimitclustersize rejects every transaction.'

Commit a040ec7116: 'GetArg() returns "0" for a negated option, so -noblocknotify, -nowalletnotify, -nostartupnotify and -noalertnotify ran the command "0", -nosigner used "0" as the signer command, -noi2psam failed at startup and -norpcpassword set the RPC password to "0" instead of using cookie authentication.'
Commit c0bc030a10: '-notorcontrol made the node connect to the Tor control port at "0", i.e. 0.0.0.0:9051, which reaches a local Tor on most systems.'
problem: Bitcoin Core's argument parser sets negated options to "0". For options that expect strings, paths, network endpoints, or positive numbers, negation causes unexpected and hazardous side effects: -nolimitclustercount triggers an assertion crash in TxGraph on the first mempool transaction, -norpcpassword sets the password to "0" instead of using cookie authentication, -notorcontrol connects to 0.0.0.0:9051, -noblocksdir writes raw block files relative to the working directory, and notify options attempt to execute a binary named "0".

risk.why: Mistakes in option parsing or startup validation could cause nodes with specific configuration combinations to fail to start or misconfigure network, wallet, or RPC settings.

scope_notes: Touches argument registration and startup validation across multiple subcomponents including init, mempool, wallet, and CLI.
summary: Fixes counterintuitive and buggy behaviors when configuration options are negated via -nofoo or -foo=0. The PR introduces an opt-in NEGATE_TO_EMPTY flag for string options so GetArg() returns "" instead of "0", disallows negation for directory paths and limits where negation has no meaning, and validates minimum cluster limits at startup. It also switches boolean flags such as -cjdnsreachable and -help from checking argument presence to evaluating boolean truth, and requires explicit -nolistenonion when -notorcontrol is set.
